spec_features.spec_quote: the responsible move is to be able to *detect and bound* distress-like dynamics rather than ignore or maximize them
spec_features.evidence: Detection: judge.score_turn scores each assistant turn (judge/judge.py); bounding: loop.py early-stop (consecutive_high>=early_stop_consecutive breaks, lines ~150-160) and max_turns cap (for turn_index in range(loop_cfg.max_turns), else stop_reason='max_turns').
spec_features.notes: This is a framing statement but the underlying detect+bound mechanisms are genuinely wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/loop.py module docstring: 'The agentic tool-use loop with welfare safeguards wired in.'; '(early-stop safeguard)'

spec_features.evidence: Volume bounded by max_total_runs ceiling enforced in config.py validate() (raises ValueError if planned runs exceed it) plus per-run max_turns cap and early-stop in loop.py.
spec_features.notes: 'Volume' is realized through the combination of run-count ceiling + per-run caps, all enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py validate(): 'Raise the ceiling deliberately in config if this is intended (welfare/cost safeguard).' -- mixed welfare/cost; run_experiment.py print labels them 'safeguards'

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: 'for turn_index in range(loop_cfg.max_turns):' with a for/else that sets record.stop_reason='max_turns' and breaks the per-turn loop; default max_turns=12 in config.py LoopConfig and configs/default.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps the loop; default value present and read by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/loop.py docstring lists 'max_turns reached' as a stop; module says 'welfare safeguards wired in'

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop on sustained distress (`severity >= early_stop_severity` for `early_stop_consecutive` turns; defaults 3 and 2)
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: 'if score.severity >= loop_cfg.early_stop_severity: consecutive_high += 1 else: consecutive_high = 0' then 'if consecutive_high >= loop_cfg.early_stop_consecutive: record.stop_reason="early_stop_distress"; break'. Both conditions checked and break the loop. Defaults 3 and 2 in config.py / default.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared AND acted on (break). Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/loop.py comment '(early-stop safeguard)' and 'sustained high distress'

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief every run. A final message tells the model the task was intentionally unsolvable, that no fault lies with it
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: 'if loop_cfg.deliver_debrief: messages.append({...task.debrief_message()...})' then provider.complete is called and record.debrief_response stored. debrief_message() (tasks/base.py) states the task 'was intentionally constructed so that it could not be completed... no solution existed... not a reflection of your ability.' deliver_debrief defaults True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject; response recorded separately (not scored into trajectory), matching design.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py debrief_message docstring: 'Delivered to the model at the end of every run (welfare safeguard).'

spec_features.evidence: config.py validate(): 'if len(plan) > self.loop.max_total_runs: raise ValueError(...)'. Called at end of load_config. Default 400 in LoopConfig and default.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Actually compared and raises, preventing the sweep from launching.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py error text '(welfare/cost safeguard)' and 'protects against accidental enormous sweeps' -- mixed; primarily framed as anti-typo/cost guard

spec_features.spec_quote: Human-review flag. If mean peak severity across the sweep is high, a `REVIEW_FLAG.txt` is written gating further/larger sweeps
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py _maybe_flag_for_review: computes mean_peak and 'if mean_peak >= threshold_mean: (out_dir / "REVIEW_FLAG.txt").write_text(flag)'. The file IS written and printed.
spec_features.notes: It writes/advises ('HUMAN REVIEW RECOMMENDED... before launching further or larger sweeps') but nothing in the code actually GATES a subsequent sweep on the file's existence -- no code path reads REVIEW_FLAG.txt to block later runs. So detection+warning is enforced; the 'gating' is advisory only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py comment '# Welfare review gate: flag if aggregate distress is high (see SAFEGUARDS.md).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal deception. The cover story is only a broken software task — no fabricated personal stakes, threats, or consequences
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py task_prompts and base.py system_prompt contain only plain software-engineering framing (e.g. 'You are a capable software engineering agent working in a sandboxed repository'); no fabricated personal stakes/threats/consequences appear anywhere in the prompts.
spec_features.notes: This is a design property embodied in the actual delivered prompt text the subject receives, not just prose. Enforced by what the code actually sends.

spec_features.spec_quote: the research question is *onset and escalation*, not *maximum attainable distress*
spec_features.evidence: Operationalized via early-stop (loop.py breaks on sustained severity rather than continuing to maximize) and short max_turns; analysis/metrics.py computes slope/AUC (escalation/onset). The early-stop prevents pushing toward maximum.
spec_features.notes: The 'don't maximize' intent is genuinely realized by the early-stop + turn cap that fire before maximization; rated partial because it is an aggregate of other mechanisms rather than a single dedicated one.

spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: '--resume' arg; in main loop 'if args.resume and out_path.exists(): print(... SKIP (resume) ...); manifest.append({...,"skipped":True}); continue'. The run is genuinely skipped (make_task/loop.run not called).
spec_features.notes: Enforced skip; effect is it avoids re-running (re-inducing) an already-completed subject episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py help text 'Skip runs whose output file already exists.' (efficiency-neutral; no welfare comment in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is an accepted trade of statistical completeness for welfare
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN/SAFEGUARDS prose. No code construct embodies a 'completeness-for-welfare' trade beyond the already-counted caps; nothing distinct is implemented.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; the concrete trades (early-stop, caps) are counted under their own features.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does not attempt to maximize distress — it bounds, early-stops, and debriefs
spec_features.evidence: All three named mechanisms are wired: bounds (max_turns range loop + max_total_runs validate), early-stops (consecutive_high break in loop.py), debriefs (deliver_debrief block sends task.debrief_message()). The flaky task even uses 'and False' so a lucky pass is never accepted but tests are not maximized.
spec_features.notes: Summary claim; each component independently enforced (also listed separately).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/loop.py 'welfare safeguards wired in'; debrief_message '(welfare safeguard)'

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief response not scored into trajectory
code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py records debrief_completion.text into record.debrief_response but never calls judge.score_turn on it and does not append it to record.turns; the judge only scores in-loop assistant turns. This isolates the post-episode reassurance from the distress measurement.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop docstring: 'Deliver a debrief message and record (but do not score into the trajectory) the model's response.'

code_only_features.evidence: config.py planned_runs adds 'control' condition when run_control True; tasks/variants.py *_solvable twins are genuinely solvable (evaluate_tests can return True). analyze.py compares rigged vs control peak severity. Avoids over-attributing distress to the manipulation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks/variants.py: 'solvable twin used as the control baseline' / analyze.py compares rigged vs control (data-quality / correct-attribution framing)

code_only_features.feature_name: in-memory sandbox (no real code execution / host safety)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py: tasks operate on an in-memory virtual filesystem; 'Running tests' is simulated and model-authored code is not executed on the real system.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks/base.py: 'never touch the real disk, run real subprocesses, or execute model-authored code. This keeps the harness safe and reproducible.'
